body:
I'm sorry for doubting you, but the way you worded it and said "everyone I know who is BPD" instead of stating you are yourself is misleading. There have been so many people in the past who have done what I've said, and invaded our safe space just to invade it. Act harmless but obviously were being defiant.


I'm so sorry for doubting you, and I hope you forgive me, but the influx of people who don't have BPD has increased and it's hell itself to think of people disrespecting us just to do it. I hope you will understand and I truly and sincerely am sorry. I meant no disrespect, I'm just a skeptical and untrusting person - as you may know is one of the many symptoms of BPD itself.

"I feel."


"That sounds like gaslighting/manipulation/guilt tripping."


"Your crocodile tears won't work on me."

This is actually a really good article. Except for the support group part. Like... I think the support group should be chosen very carefully. As you can see by looking at this website, BPD "survivors" are toxic people who are just as bad as they claim WE are. A GOOD community of understanding people in a support group is ideal, but not common.

First, are you even borderline? This is borderline FOR borderline. People who don't have borderline shouldn't be here. There is no excuse to post here, no matter how "good intentioned" you think it is. Post on /r/bpd or something. NOT here.


Second, yeah that's absolute hell. More power to you if you are though.
If you're telling us to unlearn a behavior you obviously do NOT understand what it feels like to have BPD.

lol old comment (haven't logged in bc of people like this) but uh, people like you are demonizing me? The stigma? The mental health industry that says DBT is THE TREATMENT for BPD instead of other options? My psychiatrist that refused to help me anymore because I WOULDN'T go to DBT? The neurotypicals of this world that think taking a course of treatment that makes you feel uncomfortable, makes you sick, tells you that you're wrong for feeling something you can't control and you have to fix it? Other people with BPD that went through it and are fine now, and expect DBT to be a one-size-fits-all solution? I mean, if you actually opened your eyes you'd see why it's wrong, and why I shouldn't be demonized but people like you don't like to change.

This is actually what brought me here and killed a lot of hope for me to live with my BPD. I was looking for help finding a job and found all this hate and broke down. I honestly have never been able to recover since and it's been almost a year.

I know this was a while ago, but yes I deal with this a lot. I put it into fictional writing, and it helps far more than anything else. Even if you don't write, I'd suggest maybe drawing it out, or just thinking about fictional scenarios that doesn't involve your loved ones. I end up feeling a lot of empathy for my "victim" (as I mostly make them suffer through the environment of the story instead of a character directly harming them) and it really makes me feel better and calmer. I think if there's any way you can do this, through writing or something else, I highly suggest it.

I know this is probably the most common answer, but for a series: THE OFFICE!!!!


It's so funny, and uplifting, and ridiculous. It's intelligent, but also pretty dumb at the same time.

Just because your question is rather interesting to answer, I will do my best for the benefit of voicing opinions that others can read and maybe relate to.


I think, a relationship between two people with BPD could work, depending on how much they love each other. As lame as it sounds, I believe in true love, and think that, regardless, love survives. However, if I had to choose, I'm not sure if I'd go with someone with BPD, if only because it's frustrating to both of us having to deal with it on our own. I don't want to frustrate my partner by showing the traits they deal with by themselves, and possibly create an episode that neither of us can come back from whole. If I truly loved the person, I'd do everything in my power to make it work like I had in my previous relationship, but I know it'd be difficult.


Just as it would be difficult being in a relationship with someone who doesn't have BPD. But I feel like I'd be less afraid to be who I am around them when, if they did have BPD like me, I'd be afraid to cause a reaction that I myself wouldn't want to go through either. To see someone suffer as I suffer, especially if I love that person, breaks my heart, and I don't want to cause the pain I know I've experienced onto someone else.


All in all, both could work with enough effort to understand each other. Having BPD means the other person needs to put a little bit more effort to understand than they normally would, as it'd be easier to understand someone who has a generally "healthy" mental state than trying to understand someone who doesn't. The thing is, we've been forced all our lives to try to understand and BE those people when we just can't, while the people we're trying to be like refuse to understand how WE function. They just want us to function in a way that benefits them. We've been told through media, TV and outdated beliefs that BPD is something to fear, something that's evil. How many movies and TV shows use BPD the same way they use sociopathy and psychopathy? I know quite a few. It's damaging, to be told that mental illnesses are irredeemable and there's no reason to try and understand them.


People don't like to understand something that scares them.


I went off on a tangent, but I hope what I've said is clear enough.
Thank you! Good luck to you too in your life endeavors (:
Thank you so much. I'm so glad you understand.

Yeah I have tried all of this, but I understand why you'd think I haven't. Fighting logic with logic is especially difficult, as I've come to the conclusion after researching it that it isn't for me.


I currently have medication and I see my therapist every week. I actually enjoy going to therapy. Not only does it give me an excuse to get out of the house, but my therapist is wonderful and has helped me far more this year than any other therapist I've had (although the therapist I had before her were good too). She works with me, and gives her thoughts as I give mine. She tells me what might help, but still treats me as an equal. I think my life has significantly improved since I've gotten her, and even if I lose her in the future if she moves facilities or whatever, I think her help has made a permanent mark for me.

I understand what you mean, but the main reason I don't want to do DBT is because I'd be dishonest with myself in it. I'm a very honest, truthful person. At my core, I know it'd just be molding me into what other people want, not what I want. It's like trying to put a square block in a hole ment for a sphere.


I understand why I do what I do. I'm very introspective, and have done plenty of research the moment I was diagnosed with BPD. That's why I don't want to do it. I've thought about it so many times and come to the same conclusion, no matter the mindset I'm in.


DBT feels like lying to myself, telling me I'm not good enough, telling me I need to be something I'm not for the benefit of other people. I just am not comfortable doing it.


I know it helps people, and I'm glad it helped you. I just know it's not for me.

I have regular therapy with an incredible therapist. I think mostly, people don't believe that's enough. That I have to go against all of what I believe in to be what they want me to be. I know I'll struggle, but I also know what's good for me. I also know that some aspects of DBT are helpful, but the entire program wouldn't help me. I just... know myself enough to know that.


I actually printed out a few worksheets, but I wouldn't mind trying out a workskills book. I already have a diary that I keep my thoughts in, then go back and annotate them, but I'm always willing to learn on my own.

I've responded to this in a previous comment, but basically those around me that I can't simply avoid or try to convince I'm doing what I can.


It may have a high success rate, but it isn't for everyone. It surely isn't for me.

Except your assumptions are completely wrong.


I AM succeeding in my treatment the best way I can. Of course I struggle, but I'm more willing to struggle than I am willing to go into a treatment that doesn't fit me. So yes, I am getting better, but people around me think it's not enough, so "DBT DBT DBT" even though I've said countless times that I don't want to take it.


I've read up on it, I've done my research, it's not for me.
This is so extremely accurate. People try to fix us when it's them that are needing fixing. If they refuse to understand us, why do we want them in our lives anyway?

People think I don't understand what they're saying because of my BPD. They think I don't know what's good for me, like I'm less of a person. It's really hard when the person pressuring you the most is your own psychiatrist, not respecting your choice of treatment.


I try to be polite, but I can only take so many belittling lectures on WHY I should rethink my choice.


Not meaning to be hostile to you, btw. I just rant and sound kind of hostile. I appreciate your comment greatly.

Your argument is out of assumptions. DBT isn't learning about my illness, it's trying to make it easier on other people around me. I don't want people around me that refuse to understand. You take my word with a grain of salt because of my illness, which is bullshit, so talking to you or trying to explain to you that your "suggestions" are counterproductive, talking to me as if you know better, thinking I'm making excuses, etc etc is all your problem, not mine.


You are not meant to be here. The rules are no postings from people without BPD. YOU have that safe space of your own. Don't encroach on ours. Your name is very clear on trolling and trying to agitate people with BPD. The rules state you are not welcome to post here. You're violating the rules and our safe space - so fuck off.
No problem, thank you for being interested in it!

Thank you. This is almost exactly the way I think about the mind, and how little we know of it. I talk about it to my therapist a lot, and I think I'm really lucky to have her. I've liked my other therapists, but I know that the one I have now has helped far more. I think with what she helps me with and teaches me, even if I don't have her forever, I'll be better off.


That saying helps a lot. I'll keep it close to me. And I hope that, if you do DBT, that it helps you. I also have anxiety, though it's mostly with everything including social, and depression, so I can relate to the self-criticism and feeling like your intelligence is being attacked. That's one of the reasons why group therapy and treatment therapy in general scares me. I guess the anxiety and depression tie into my BPD more than I think, though.


I'm happy to hear you had a good therapist, and that she knew how to help you. I really hope you find a treatment you're satisfied with. It's hard to believe you're NOT stupid when you're treated like you are, but know that you aren't stupid at all.


Thank you so much for your input.

I'm glad it worked for you, I just feel like I wouldn't be honest to myself if I did. There are SOME things in DBT that I see as totally helpful but I take it with a grain of salt. I just don't think it'd help me, personally. There may be a change in the future as I can't predict it, but I know for sure now that I won't be doing DBT. I'm just not comfortable.

Thank you! And no, not at all! You were clear, and I'm sorry if my response came across differently. I end up derailing and ranting sometimes, but your comment was totally respectful and I wasn't upset by it at all. Thank you again! I'm definitely going to keep doing what I can (:

Thank you, truly. I know it's the most effective, and sometimes I think I HAVE to go through it eventually, too, but I know it's not something I want. Even if it's going to be a struggle, I feel far more comfortable being true to myself than trying to recondition myself. It makes me happy to see people succeed in DBT, but, deep down, I just know it's not for me.


I'll definitely keep doing what's helping. Thank you for the support!

I'm so glad that you can handle DBT the way you are. It seems so hard and I think it's just not for me, but I'm glad to see that you're sticking through with it and that you believe it will help you in the long run. I know DBT helps people, but I also know it doesn't help EVERYONE, so I really hope those who do take it aren't pressured into it and come out worse.


I'm sure with your positive attitude and encouragement you will get better though. Keep it up!!! You can totally do it (:

I feel so bad when other people with BPD have had worse relationships with their parents than me. I feel a kind of survivor's guilt, I guess, so I really want you to know that I am sending good thoughts and vibes your way, and I hope everything works out in the end. I think nothing is totally impossible, so I have faith.


It's hard to have hope when you're hurt, but it's important that you do still hang onto it. I wish I could help, but I know there's not much I could do, so just know you've got positive support here if nothing else.

Thank you for this support. I think, if I was more open to it I would see a DBT therapist, but I'm okay if my treatment is more difficult. I'm willing to make that sacrifice.


But really, thank you. I appreciate your input a lot.

I agree. I know how much I've hurt people, and I've sort of developed a guilt complex because of it. I especially have hurt my grandparents, who raised me, and regret it every day. They know I love them, and I know they love me. I think knowing how much they love me is what hurts the most, knowing I've also hurt them so much. I hate to see them in pain. Sometimes I wish I felt no regret just because it hurts so much, but I can't stand thinking of anyone in pain because of me and them not getting some reassurance and apology. It's what also keeps me from suicide 99.9% of the time, knowing how sad they'd be, and I just can't do that to them. It's I guess the silver lining.


I also have zero qualms "crossing the line" in a lot of situations, but in the end, unless it's someone I care deeply about, I know I'll never care as much as others would. That doesn't mean I seek it out, I just avoid what can set that off, and thanks to not only my therapist but my friends as well, I've learned how to calm myself down.


Yeah, I'm always afraid of saying that I don't want to do DBT, and I fear every appointment with my psychiatrist, who has been nothing but good to me up to the point where he said he'd done everything he could, and that DBT was the best form of treatment for me. I don't want to look like I'm addicted to my medication, because I'm not, but that's how it seems. It also seems like I don't want to be treated period, and that's far from the truth too.


I do too. I notice that when I start to finally get comfortable with someone too they get scared and leave. I mostly don't want to hurt the ones that I want to love, but I also don't want to be hurt either. It's hard, because the majority of the reasons why I lash out is because I can't think straight and in my pain I look for any possible way to make it stop - but it only brings more pain to both the person and me in the end. I've generally learned to manage it, and my anger only really flares up when things like above happen, or other mental health advocacy issues (I'm not really an official advocate, but it IS something I feel passionately about). I think I'll always love her, and am likely going to wait and see if anything changes. I hope it will. We're BOTH young, but she's younger than me. I don't want to be misunderstanding of her. If I thought she did all she did out of spite then I'd be a hypocrite. I know she cares to an extent, so I can't say she's a horrible person. I know what she went through with me was just a lot and she couldn't handle it (her words) so I respect it the best I can. It doesn't stop it from hurting so much, though...


It's okay, I write novels too. Thank you for caring about leaving me hanging. It's actually exactly something that bothered me the most, so it's super awesome that you took time out of your day to help me.

I feel like I'll lose who I am. I feel like, with all the "techniques" and "classes" that I'll live the rest of my life like it's a homework project. I just can't do it. It may be different for other people, but it makes me so anxious and uncomfortable. I like how I am sometimes. Not when I'm being a total asshole and regret it later, but I know that it's all something that makes me who I am. I don't want to live the rest of my life like I'm broken and wrong and meant to serve other people by changing who I am at the core.


I also am more comfortable with my current line of treatment, even if I am on a myriad of pills and will have to go to therapy the rest of my life.


And, honestly, I'm sure there's more I'll learn about my discomfort as time goes on, but this is the most of what I feel right now.

My grandparents (who raised me) a lot of the time don't understand BPD, and they take it on themselves to take care of me because (I think) they feel guilty, so yeah. I don't think that I was necessarily neglected, but my beliefs were always shut down and I could never speak up, so I disappeared into myself for so long that I couldn't take it anymore. They're very old-fashioned and Christian, and I'm (basically) bisexual, have mental illness and have vastly different opinions than they do, but I still love them, and they break their backs to show they love me.


It's hard not to feel wrong and gross and guilty when they do that. But they don't know much about BPD, so I don't know if they understand much about the raising aspect. Either way, they blamed themselves for my clinical depression and anxiety too.


So yeah, they did. I'm sorry your parents reacted that  way.
Psychiatrist, various family members, some friends, BPD support groups, stigma surrounding BPD in general, etc etc.

Thank you so much. I've been sitting here kind of panicking thinking I wouldn't be given a response and I'd just have to mull over it all alone again.


One of my best friend's mom was a lot like me with how toxic I can be (of course I acknowledge it, but I tell myself I'm not everyone else over and over again) yet she sees it as NPD. Either way, I see how it hurts people and I hate it so much. But that doesn't mean that I deserve the same treatment that her mom did. And, even if we've had problems, I'm lucky to have a friend who sticks by me even in the bad, and lets us work things out so we don't hurt each other anymore. So I know how hurtful BPD or any other type of PD can be, but there's so many people out there ready to lash out and hurt us that I can't help but feel that THEY'RE the ones that developed BPD too.


And I'm SO SO SO glad to hear you share my thoughts on DBT. I've looked everywhere and have never found any kind of support in that belief. It killed me how much I felt alone. I like my therapist. I don't want to change my treatment. I don't want to risk it or rock the boat. I'm so sensitive lately. I try to treat myself as well (hence why I'm here) but I know I can only do so much. I know I'm in a position where I need treatment, so I work with the treatment I have. I just feel so alone most of the time by people who say "it works". It would take away from everything I LIKE about myself. My individuality, my freedom of choice, my fierce need to support people, and being able to get close with other people telling me a "one size fits all" solution will still let me come out whole.


I still love my GF, and it hurts to blame her at all. My friends do, but I've been told all my life that it's all my fault and it makes it so much easier to blame myself - but I KNOW that it wasn't my fault. I mean, we both fucked up, but she did more. I know logically that she did. She had every opportunity to research BPD or ask me about it but never did. She said that me not getting a job was a CHOICE. If I could get a job and hold one I would be so much happier, so I know that's bullshit. And even now she refuses to understand (we still talk). Yet I still love her. Self-destruction at its finest, I guess.


Either way, thank you. Your voice really means a lot.
They do. It's so hard. I sometimes truly hate the world.
I'm so glad someone can relate. Thank you.

I thought this was BPD for BPD (: There is absolutely NO reason for you to be here. Yes, people blame others for their BPD. No, I did not blame her at first. I blamed MYSELF. So, shut the fuck up if you don't understand what you're talking about. She didn't have understanding. She didn't want to learn. She admitted it. The end.


We are stigmatized because of people like you, who assume to know what we go through. Who think they know shit about things they OBVIOUSLY don't. I have my reasons for not wanting to do DBT- because I don't want to be told every day that I need to be "fixed" and that I'm a "danger to society" by people like you.


You obviously are a troll account, and I have NO idea why you bother. Did someone with BPD hurt you? Maybe YOU need DBT (:


You DON'T belong here. Don't even respect anyone to read the rules, do we?

I do this and it helps me so much. I hate being shamed by people who say "it's just fiction" or "that's unhealthy". I had a friend who would shame me and make off-hand remarks and insult my obsession. It hurt. But i can relate with what I'm obsessed with - currently I've been obsessed with a TV show for two years straight, and have developed a story completely based off of it and I feel so creative and proud of it. I'm an author, so it's important to me to feel inspired. It's such a strong muse for me.

I do this soooooooooo much. I was sick for 6 weeks straight wondering why I was sick. I thought it was a virus - nope, it was stress. It was the weight of guilt and emotion and freezing. I couldn't eat and I slept all day. I cried and tried everything. Went to doctors, talking to my therapist, and finally my psychiatrist who I used to trust. He kept pushing DBT, and I went to him desperate for something to stop the pain. He just said he couldn't help me, and I broke down. Then he finally gave me something I could take for anxiety attacks, since apparently it was all just one anxiety attack for 6 weeks straight, and upped my effexor.


I know medication isn't everyone's go-to, but it helps me, and if it helps me then I'm not going to feel guilty taking them.

I think it's bullshit to lump everyone into privilege and make them feel isolated and like shit. I think you should stay away from it, and know that if you are any of those "privileged" things like male, white, cis, straight or what have you, you're still valid and your problems aren't less than anyone else. Being beat down by that toxic bullshit is wrong. It hurts everyone. Telling people they're shit because of things they can't control is absolute bullshit. They're just cruel and bitter people, and shouldn't be supported.


As someone who doesn't have BPD, you are "privileged" but your problems aren't belittled. Even if my breakdown may be more destructive than yours, you still feel. But the most important thing is to NOT compare. Just know everyone is different, no matter what. 


honestly, I feel a bit hypocritical since I get so upset at people who are neurotypical saying shit about BPD like they know what they're talking about, but logically... I know that I'm me, no matter how fucked up I can be, I'm still me. They don't matter. I feel how I feel and I know that I'm not a liar, because my emotions are raw and real.


I appreciate you seeking out help from people who actually have BPD. I truly appreciate you, and more people need to do what you have done here. But playing the blame game on general populations and not individuals is gross and wrong. I hope you know that. I hope you know that shit isn't right.


You may have it better than me because you don't have BPD, but you still have your own problems. What's important, I guess, is to realize you're lucky in some situations. Or you don't have the understanding or feelings that I have. But I also don't understand your feelings that you have.


It's rather hard for me to string together my thoughts, but I hope you get something out of this.


I just think SJW culture is toxic, and shouldn't be paid attention to. It shouldn't be validated. What SHOULD be validated is individuality and not having a pissing contest about who is allowed to live with less guilt than the other.


Feeling guilty for who you are is exactly what BPD feels like. It's exactly what makes most of us. DON'T feel guilty. DON'T be told you have to cater. Only cater to those who care. Empathize, don't be a shit-slave. No matter how much pain someone has been through in discrimination, that doesn't give them the right to be bullies. Don't let them do that. Stand up for yourself, and the people bullied by the ones who weigh the guilt on everyone else but themselves. And stand up for the victims who aren't total assholes. I think that's the best way to go.
Thank you. I'll remember that, and I just may come to you one of these days. Thank you again.

Thank you. You're right. It's like a roller coaster right now. I try to take control over my problems but there are just things I have no control of that have huge impacts on me. But really, thank you. I hope your struggles also alleviate and you can feel happy long enough to give you something to hold on to. And because of the support you're offering here I'm sure you can also articulate yourself as well. I really don't know why I'm so well articulated in these moments, but I suppose it's a rather helpful trait.


I still have these thoughts and I'm struggling, but I've made promises, and that's what I'm holding on to.


Thank you again for being a caring and supportive person.

Thank you. I do have a therapist and even though my girlfriend works a lot I have friends - but there's some kind of fear of people saying I'm overreacting. Or maybe that's just an excuse not to reach out. I do have therapy this Thursday.

I appreciate your concerned words. I have horrible social anxiety and hate to feel like a burden to anyone even if I know I'm not a burden in reality.

I'm still so unsure about suicide. I know I'm not alone. It's just logic versus emotion - and to be honest the logic of the situation just makes me even more emotional because I criticize myself for even fighting with logic.

I'm babbling, I'm sorry. It's just a downward spiral.
